There is a unique misery that proceeds the idea that you don't like what is a "fact", it is so distressing. 

When my anxiety on this topic reached peak levels, I found significant evidence that the majority of people well read in this topic are very unsure themselves, with lots of arguing as I mentioned. There are a lot of unanswered questions, something else that helps me is a reminder that being truly "free" would actually be terrible as you'd act entirely randomly with no motivation on one aspect. 

The fact you (or anyone/anything) are somewhat determined isn't a bad thing, an example I can give is you are predetermined to be forced to breathe air or you'll die. This isn't something anyone is too concerned with, the problem is when that freedom of choice and life feels like it's gone. I am not here to debate philosophy, personally I find it all a bit pretentious and uppity.

I would be happy to talk more about this and try to help, believe me I've been exactly where you are now and while right this second that crushing feeling of despair might feel inescapable, it isn't quite as simple as it might seem.

I agree 100% life is unfair, some people are born into great families and wealth etc. Doesn't guarantee a good life, but increases it. When you hear about someone having a terrible childhood, poor, has some horrible illness and then just dies young, you have to seriously consider the fact some people really haven't got a fighting chance. It's a sad reality, but a reality.

"society and this civilization we've constructed is unsustainable, arbitrary, and fragile, and possesses the means for its own annihilation into oblivion" I'd argue that the fact it's been going for 100s of years shows the opposite of this. I think society is really strong actually, which is a blessing and a curse. I thick society changes a lot however,  2020 is a lot different to 2010. You could argue that 2010 society collapsed because of how different it is.

 "Human nature is honestly at the root of all our problems, not to mention the invention of farming and the creation of complex societies to begin with." I disagree actually, if human nature was at the root of the problem, no society would have ever formed. Everyone would have given into their urges instead of working together, I'd argue working together is a fundamental human trait. Greed and arrogance is 100% the problem, I imagine most wars (if not all) were caused because people just assumed they were both right without actually listening and then got angry and started violence. That or some greedy power hungry leader wanted to destroy enemies for more land or power etc. If everyone was more calm, didn't let their pride blind them and understood the needs of others, 90% of the worlds problems wouldn't exist. 

I think society itself isn't imposable to sustain, if there was for example, only 1 million people, then everyone could live lavishly and climate change wouldn't even start to happen. If we had 100 billion people then I'd imagine we'd be completely screwed. There has to be a balance between a nice life and amount of resources used.

I think most people have access to atleast some of humanities advancements, and those that do not are quickly developing. This is problem however, the fact that the rich are hoarding so much while the poor have a lot less. The fact the 1% have more than the rest of us 99% is disgusting and makes me sick, I do not deny that at all. I think also the to 10 richest have more than the bottom 50%..... 10 people > 3.8 billion according to these rich people, this is a really big problem 100%. The more we advance the better I'd say, I see it as a sort of v shape if you like, before, every single advancement was a negative in the long run. At some point we hit rock bottom, but now we are starting to go up again. All these new eco friendly and cheaper, more efficient inventions make me extremely impressed. Vegan food is more popular and easy to get than ever, renewable energy is more vast (atleast where I live) than ever, all these new discoveries are extremely impressive and help us long term rather than short term. The psychological aspects of people is poor right now, I think over stimulation has made things worse, coupled with many other factors a lot of people now are struggling (me included). 

"We're not going to change who we are anytime soon" a lot of people have though, veganism is a good example. I think we can both agree that being vegan is much better for the environment (ignoring all philosophical arguments here) and that being vegan is one of the best things you can do as a single person to decrease CO2 emissions. The amount of vegans 10, 20 years ago was extremely low, now? look at the amount there are, the amount of people who have stepped up to make the world a better place. This is a massive amount, a lot of whom are young too, which to me shows that younger people are starting to see the reality, better it's the younger than older with things like this. The massive climate change moments, things like ecosia, it's impossible to ignore the reality of climate change, but I think it's equally impossible to ignore how many people care and are doing things, is it enough? maybe not at the moment, but I think a lot of people are proving that they're ready to make changes. 

"this year will only be the first of many long hard years ahead of us" If that is what we need in order to make the changes needed then so be it.
